Definition: from G4862 and G1957; to testify further jointly, i.e. unite in adding evidence:--also bear witness.
BiblicalUsage: The writer of Hebrews says God also bears witness with signs and wonders and diverse miracles and gifts of the Holy Ghost, according to His own will. God's witness is not a word alone but wonders added to the word, and the Spirit's gifts are His signature on the message.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that God bears witness to His own word with signs and wonders, and I hold that the gospel needs no better witness than the God who confirms it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
